A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from R0 to Reward-Instruct. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and support matching across revisions, including v2's appendices. v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated-image evaluations in Table 1, training diagnostics, regularization and reward ablations, and downstream application examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds baseline results, measured training costs, reward correlations, and SGLD and reward-choice experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces the gradient-based update with an explicit SGLD update containing Gaussian parameter noise; Reward-Instruct+ also adopts this update. This introduces parameter-distribution sampling and a substantive regularization component. The unrolled generator, random-eta sampling, normalized reward gradients, weight anchoring, intermediate supervision and high-resolution guidance otherwise remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use JourneyDB prompts, COCO-5k and HPS benchmark prompts, and demonstrate text-to-image generation, image editing, ControlNet conditioning and Dreamshaper compatibility. The new reward and SGLD analyses use retained coverage rather than introducing a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds ReFL and DRaFT as evaluated reward-centric, 50-NFE alternatives, substantially broadening the principal comparison beyond fast distillation-based methods. They also participate in the new training-cost comparison. Hyper-SD, RG-LCM and DI++ remain, while the Referee can play comparison moves to Appendix A.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a training-cost protocol using equal batch sizes and iteration counts on RTX-4090, an alternative reward configuration, SGLD-on/off comparisons, and reward-correlation measurement on COCO-5k. Existing benchmark metrics remain. Table 1 changes the Steps heading to NFE and re-expresses base-model counts; this alone does not establish changed sampling budgets or reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-efficiency analysis, an SGLD randomness ablation under larger reward weights, aesthetic-reward substitution, and reward-correlation analysis (Tables 2–4 and Figure 15). It expands the eta sweep but removes v1's gradient-cosine analysis in Figure 6. Existing weight-regularization, reward-combination, convergence, generation-path and high-resolution analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces Pearson correlation estimation between reward scores on COCO-5k in Table 4, a statistical analysis absent from v1. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 quality scores are unchanged, but v2 adds ReFL/DRaFT results, training costs and reward correlations. Table 2 reports 28 GPU-hours for Reward-Instruct, versus 36 for DI++ and 20 for RG-LCM. Table 3's alternative reward configuration improves FID from 33.79 to 31.26 while reducing HPS from 33.70 to 32.35, a configuration tradeoff rather than a same-setting gain. New SGLD examples and revised sample panels add qualitative results; the old gradient-cosine finding disappears.

T1.justification: v2 adds an image-likelihood constraint, a reward-tilted parameter posterior, a Gaussian prior around pretrained parameters, and the SGLD derivation in Section 3.2.2. These substantially extend v1's reward-maximization formulation and explicit weight penalty. No convergence proof is added. The new constraint p(x) <= c in Equations 3.1 and 3.5 conflicts with the accompanying explanation that low-likelihood images should be excluded.

C1.justification: The central claim that regularized rewards enable high-quality four-step generation without diffusion distillation remains. v2 adds an explicit abstract-level claim of sampling from a reward-tilted parameter distribution and emphasizes training-efficiency and stability benefits in the introduction. These extend the contribution claims while preserving the central thesis.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies dependence on differentiable rewards and leaves black-box rewards and non-diffusion generators unexplored. It interprets SGLD noise as protection against repeated-object artifacts and proposes reward complementarity as an explanation for the aesthetic-reward configuration's FID improvement. The interpretation based on declining gradient cosine similarity is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies AdamW, beta values 0.9 and 0.95, learning rate 2e-5 and batch size 256; Table 2 adds hardware and GPU-hour information. These are new disclosures, not evidence that existing settings changed. Conversely, v2 removes v1's code-availability statement and repository link.

R1.justification: The introduction, Remark 3.1 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against reward-driven alternatives, including shortcut fine-tuning, Adjoint Matching and ReNO, and connect the formulation to reward-weighted reinforcement learning and SGLD. v2 explicitly distinguishes parameter-space from image-space reward tilting and claims the first direct conversion without distillation or training images. Existing diffusion and preference-alignment surveys are retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and R0/R0+ become Reward-Instruct/Reward-Instruct+. The phase-transition argument moves into the method section, the method presentation is reorganized, evaluation gains dedicated subsections, and related work, pseudocode and implementation details move into appendices. Some editing remains unfinished, including an 'Appendix ??' reference.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive figure rearrangement and resizing. v2 replaces most teaser samples, adds Tables 2–4 and the SGLD figure, removes the gradient-cosine plot, and restructures Table 1 with method categories and NFE reporting. The Referee comparison and Algorithm 1 are relocated to the appendices.

improvement.justification: The added reward-centric baselines, training-cost comparison and targeted ablations strengthen the empirical case, while implementation settings and explicit limitations improve assessability. The gains are limited by removal of the code link, the contradictory likelihood constraint, and an AdamW description that is not reconciled with the stated SGLD algorithm. Overall, the additional evidence and reporting provide a modest net improvement despite these unresolved defects.
